cues.zh: 既然大家已经大致了解了我们在 Reddit 上做的架构决策，
cues.en: Now that you've got a pretty good idea of the architecture decisions we made on Reddit

cues.zh: 以及我们随着时间推移如何拓展网站规模并改变数据存储方式，
cues.en: and how we kind of grew the site and stored data differently over time,

cues.zh: 接下来我想聊聊我们实际上是如何从社交层面做大这个网站的——
cues.en: what I'd like to talk about is now we actually grew the site from a social point of view--

cues.zh: 也就是我们如何获取用户，以及如何保持 Reddit 独有的社区氛围。
cues.en: how we got users and how we maintained the feel that Reddit has.

cues.zh: 我和其他任何人都很难把 Reddit 的成长归功于自己，
cues.en: It's hard for me or anybody to really take credit for growing Reddit,

cues.zh: 因为这是个社交产品，即便我和 Alexis 带着现在的全套认知在今天重新做一遍，
cues.en: because it's a social thing and even if Alexis and I started over today knowing everything

cues.zh: 也很难让像 Reddit 这样的网站成功起步。
cues.en: we know now, it'd be very hard to get a site like Reddit off the ground.

cues.zh: 社交类网站要想做起来，需要一点运气的“魔法”，而我们足够幸运拥有了它。
cues.en: Social websites require a little bit of magic to work, and we were fortunate enough to have it.

cues.zh: 不过我认为我们确实做了很多极其重要且有所帮助的事，
cues.en: We did a lot of very important things that I think helped,

cues.zh: 其中之一就是，刚开始时所有的内容都是我和 Alexis 亲自分享提交的。
cues.en: one of which was in the beginning Alexis and I submitted all the content.

cues.zh: 如果你现在去 Reddit 的发帖页面，基本上就简化成了两个输入框。
cues.en: If you go to our Reddit submission page now, it basically boils down to two fields.

cues.zh: 早期也只有两个输入框。
cues.en: In the early days it was just two fields.

cues.zh: 基本上就是一个叫“URL”的输入框，也就是你要提交的网站链接，
cues.en: You basically had a field called "URL," which is the URL of the site you were submitting,

cues.zh: 还有一个是“Title”，也就是那个网站的标题，这就是你发到 Reddit 上的链接内容。
cues.en: and "Title," which was the title of that site, and that would be the link you submitted to Reddit.

cues.zh: 如果是我和 Alexis 访问那个页面，我们会有第三个输入框，叫做“User”，
cues.en: If Alexis and I went to the page we had a third field called "User,"

cues.zh: 我们可以在这里输入一个用户名，点击提交后，
cues.en: and we could type in a name here, and when we hit submit,

cues.zh: 如果该用户名不存在，系统就会自动注册这个用户，
cues.en: we would automatically register this user if that name didn't exist

cues.zh: 并以该用户的身份发布内容。
cues.en: and submit the content as that user.

cues.zh: 在最初的几个月里，你打开早期的 Reddit，
cues.en: You'd go to Reddit in the early days, the first couple of months,

cues.zh: 会看到海量的内容。
cues.en: and there'd be tons of content.

cues.zh: 我不能说是“假内容”，但确实是假用户。其实全都是我和 Alexis 发的。
cues.en: I shouldn't say "fake content," but it was fake users. It was really all just Alexis and I.

cues.zh: 这起到了两个作用，我认为这对任何想要营造社区氛围的网站都很重要。
cues.en: That did two things, and I think this is important to any site where you want to have a community feel.

cues.zh: 首先，它定下了基调。
cues.en: The first thing it did was it set the tone.

cues.zh: 网站是有这种惯性的，我们提交的内容
cues.en: Websites have this kind of inertia, and we submitted content

cues.zh: 都是我们自己感兴趣想看的。
cues.en: that we would be interested in seeing.

cues.zh: 这意味着 Reddit 上的内容，至少对我们和我们的同龄圈子来说，
cues.en: That meant the content on Reddit, at least for us and for our peer group,

cues.zh: 是非常棒、非常有趣的。
cues.en: it was good, interesting stuff.

cues.zh: 我们想打造一个拥有全网最有趣内容的网站，所以我们竭尽全力去搜罗，
cues.en: We wanted a site with the most interesting content online, and s owe did our best to find it

cues.zh: 然后亲自把这些内容提交上去。
cues.en: and then we submitted that content ourselves.

cues.zh: 这样当你访问 Reddit 时，大概就能明白这个网站是干什么的了。
cues.en: So when you show up to Reddit, you kind of know what the site is all about.

cues.zh: 另一个作用是让网站显得有生机。
cues.en: The other thing it did was it made the site feel alive.

cues.zh: 用户喜欢拥有参与感。
cues.en: Users like to feel a part of something.

cues.zh: 如果他们打开网站，首页却是一片空白，
cues.en: If they showed up to the website and the front page was blank,

cues.zh: 那就简直像个鬼城了。
cues.en: it just looks like a ghost town.

cues.zh: 你不想住在一座鬼城里。你更愿意住在纽约市。大多数人都是如此。
cues.en: You don't want to live in a ghost town. You'd rather live in New York City. Most people would.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么纽约市这么大，而鬼城顾名思义就不是。
cues.en: That's why New York City is so big and ghost towns, by definition, aren't.

cues.zh: 那真是幸运，我也不知道是什么让我们这么做的。
cues.en: That was really fortunate, and I don't know what made us do this.

cues.zh: 事后看来，很容易说事情就是这样发生的，
cues.en: In hindsight it's really easy to say this was how it happened,

cues.zh: 但当时我觉得我们只是为网站空空如也而感到尴尬，
cues.en: but at the time I think we were just embarrassed to have an empty website,

cues.zh: 所以我们提交了内容，然后它奏效了。
cues.en: so we submitted the content, and it worked.

cues.zh: 我记得几个月后第一天，我们不需要提交任何内容，
cues.en: I remember the first day a few months in when we didn't have to submit any content,

cues.zh: 那对我们来说是神奇的一天，因为那时我们知道网站已经能自己运转了。
cues.en: and that was such a magical day for us, because then we knew the site was working on its own.

cues.zh: 那真是太酷了。达到那一步花了一段时间。
cues.en: It was really, really cool. It took a while to get there.

cues.zh: 我们真的得靠意志力把它变成现实。
cues.en: We really kind of had to will this into existence.

cues.zh: 关于这个网站的另一件事是，它一开始没有任何评论。
cues.en: Another thing about the site is it didn't have any comments to begin with.

cues.zh: 我不知道这对我们是利是弊，纯粹只是我们当时还没顾上去写它。
cues.en: I don't know that this helped or hindered us. It was just we didn't get around to writing it.

cues.zh: 我想在这里唯一要说的是，人们看 Reddit，
cues.en: I think the only thing I want to say here is that people look at Reddit,

cues.zh: 如果你深入玩进去，很快就会发现评论区才是 Reddit 的灵魂所在。
cues.en: and if you get into it you quickly realize that the comments are what makes Reddit work.

cues.zh: 那里才是真正不可思议的社区所在。
cues.en: That's where the really incredible community lives.

cues.zh: 但在我们做评论系统之前，Reddit 就已经有了相当大的增长。
cues.en: And Reddit grew quite a bit before we even had a comment system.

cues.zh: 那是后来才加上的，这正好说明了一个网站
cues.en: That came later, and it just kind of goes to show how it's not always obvious what

cues.zh: 最重要的部分往往并不显而易见，与其把整个系统做完然后面临失败，
cues.en: the most important part of a site is, and it's better just to kind of get something online

cues.zh: 不如先做点东西上线，然后开始快速试错。
cues.en: and start experimenting with it than to build the whole system out and have it fail.

cues.zh: 我们当时没有任何分类，我们想让用户做的事就只是发链接。
cues.en: We didn't have any categorization. What we wanted users to do was submit links.

cues.zh: 我们不想让他们还得去想分类、想标签。
cues.en: We didn't want them to have to think about categories, think about tags.

cues.zh: 这些都是决策，决策越多，和网站交互就越难。
cues.en: Those are all decisions, and the more decisions you have the harder it is to interact with the site.

cues.zh: 我们网站上确实有过分类功能——我得说——大概就一天。
cues.en: We had categorization on the site--I should say--for about one day.

cues.zh: 我某天晚上加上了它，然后 Alexis 把 Reddit 上所有提交过的链接
cues.en: I added it one night, and Alexis took all the links that had ever been submitted to Reddit

cues.zh: 全都分了类，这样用户第二天早上来的时候一切就都准备好了。
cues.en: and categorized them, so when users came the next morning everything would be ready to go.

cues.zh: 我们最早的投资者兼顾问之一就问，你为什么要加分类功能。
cues.en: One of our first investors and advisers was like why did you add categorization.

cues.zh: 那把所有东西都搞砸了。把它去掉，我们就去掉了。
cues.en: That ruined everything. Get rid of it, so we did.

cues.zh: Alexis 最后——他白费了所有这些时间，但那真是个很好的建议。
cues.en: Alexis ended up--he wasted all of that time, but that was really good advice.

cues.zh: 没有分类功能，意味着用户可以直接上来提交内容。
cues.en: Not having categorization meant users could just show up and submit content.

cues.zh: 首页带来的那种偶然发现的乐趣，真的很吸引人。
cues.en: The serendipity of the front page was really interesting.

cues.zh: 我们做的另一件事就是不收集邮箱。
cues.en: Another thing we did was we didn't collect emails.

cues.zh: 当时几乎所有网站都有这样一套注册流程：
cues.en: Every site on there had this signup process

cues.zh: 你得输入邮箱地址，再去确认邮件——
cues.en: where you'd have to like enter your email address and then confirm an email--

cues.zh: 就是这一整套繁琐的操作。
cues.en: all those sets you have to do.

cues.zh: 其中有一步甚至要你切出浏览器，去打开邮件客户端，
cues.en: One of those steps involves you actually leaving your browser to go to your email program

cues.zh: 或者打开 Gmail 之类的，仅仅就为了注册个会员。
cues.en: or go to Gmail or whatever just to become a member.

cues.zh: 如果你想要用户、想要大家投稿，为什么还要设这么多门槛，
cues.en: If you want members and you want submissions, why would you add all the barriers

cues.zh: 比如强制要求填邮箱呢？
cues.en: like required email addresses?

cues.zh: 我们觉得反正也不会给用户发垃圾邮件，压根没什么邮件需要发。
cues.en: We figured we're not going to spam people. We don't have any emails to send.

cues.zh: 那我们为什么需要他们的邮箱？所以我们就不收集了。
cues.en: Why would we need their email addresses? So we didn't collect them.

cues.zh: 这让用户的注册流程快了许多，我认为这也是推动我们增长的一个因素。
cues.en: That allowed users to register that much faster, I think, was a contributing factor to our ability to grow.

cues.zh: 我们做的另一件大事是不做审查。
cues.en: Another big thing we did was no censorship.

cues.zh: 我们不在乎提交到 Reddit 的是什么内容。
cues.en: We didn't care what content was submitted to Reddit.

cues.zh: 除非是明显带有种族主义的东西，我们就随它去，尤其是当它对我们有批评意义时。
cues.en: Unless it was like overtly racist, we just let it be, especially if it was critical to us.

cues.zh: 这营造出了这种社区感，这种信任感。
cues.en: That created this kind of sense of community, this sense of trust.

cues.zh: 我认为，最终正是这一点让 Reddit 发展到如此巨大的规模，
cues.en: That's what ultimately, I think, allowed Reddit to grow to this tremendous size

cues.zh: 那就是用户信任我们，想成为这个社区的一部分。
cues.en: is the users believed in us and wanted to be a part of this community.

cues.zh: 当我们犯错时，甚至当我在密码哈希那件事上搞砸时，
cues.en: When we made mistakes, even when I goofed one the password hashing thing,

cues.zh: 比如，他们会继续支持我们，因为他们明白我们的出发点是好的。
cues.en: for example, they would stick with us because they realized our heart was in the right place.

cues.zh: 我们只是想做一个新颖有趣的网站。
cues.en: We just wanted to make a site that was new and interesting .

cues.zh: 我们不想出卖用户。我们不想毁掉这个网站。
cues.en: We didn't want to sell our users. We didn't want to ruin the site.

cues.zh: 我们只是想有好的内容。
cues.en: We just wanted to have good content.
